description: Connection-routing layer in front of the PostgreSQL clusters. HAProxy uses the Patroni REST API health checks to send writes to the leader and reads to the replicas.

panels.title: HAProxy Reachable
panels.description: Whether the exporter could read the HAProxy stats socket.

panels.title: Backends DOWN
panels.description: A backend with no healthy server — traffic for it is refused.

panels.title: Servers DOWN
panels.description: Expected to be non-zero: replicas fail the leader health check on the write backend by design.

panels.title: Queued Requests
panels.description: Requests waiting for a free backend connection slot.

panels.title: Server Health Timeline
panels.description: Flapping here means the Patroni health check is unstable, or a failover happened.

panels.title: Session Limit Utilization %
panels.description: How close the frontend is to its configured maxconn.

panels.title: New Connections / s
panels.description: A high connection rate against PostgreSQL argues for a connection pooler rather than raw TCP pass-through.

panels.title: Healthy Servers per Backend
panels.description: Dropping to 0 means the backend is completely unavailable.

panels.title: Backend Average Connect Time
panels.description: Time to establish the TCP connection to PostgreSQL.

panels.title: Retries & Redispatches / s
panels.description: Redispatches spike while HAProxy is moving traffic to a new leader.

panels.title: Health Check Failures / s
panels.description: Failed Patroni REST API health checks. Sustained failures on the write backend for every server means no leader.

panels.title: Health Check Duration
panels.description: A slow Patroni API response delays failover detection.

panels.title: CSV Parse Failures
panels.description: Failures parsing the HAProxy stats CSV — usually a version mismatch.
